2027-01-31.title: Fourth Sunday in Ordinary Time
readings: I will raise up a prophet and put my words in his mouth
O that today you would listen to his voice! Harden not your hearts
He taught them as one having authority
2027-01-31.alt: Year B. The memorial of St John Bosco is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. Tomorrow begins February; 2 February is the Presentation of the Lord. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-31.verse: They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
theo: Moses, near the end of his life, gives Israel a promise: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.” At Sinai the people had been terrified of hearing God's voice directly, so God says: “I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.” Israel waited for centuries for this prophet like Moses. The Gospel shows him walking into the synagogue at Capernaum.

On the Sabbath Jesus teaches, and the people are “astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” The scribes quoted others; Jesus speaks with his own voice: “But I say to you.” Then a man with an unclean spirit cries out: “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus rebukes him: “Be silent, and come out of him!” and the spirit leaves. The people ask: “What is this? A new teaching—with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.” His word does what it says.

The Psalm gives the response: “O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts.” Paul encourages the Corinthians to “unhindered devotion to the Lord”, praising those who give themselves wholly to God in celibacy, while honouring marriage as a true calling. Whatever our state of life, the question is the same: do we let the authoritative word of Jesus free us from what binds us? Today we would have honoured St John Bosco, who freed countless young people from the street through the word, education and love of Christ.
conn: Peter (Acts 3:22) and Stephen (Acts 7:37) apply Deuteronomy 18:15 to Jesus.
Greek exousia: power that comes from one's own being. The scribes cited rabbis; Jesus speaks as the Lawgiver.
The demon knows Jesus' identity before the disciples do; but knowledge without love is not faith (James 2:19).
Jesus silences the demons; he will reveal himself in his own way, on the cross.
Jesus' base in Galilee; the remains of a synagogue stand there today, built over an earlier one.
Priest of Turin (1815–1888), founder of the Salesians, whose schools and youth centres serve many in Kerala.
altar: At Mass the same authoritative word is proclaimed, and then the Word made flesh gives himself to us.
Before Communion we say: Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed. We trust the power of his word.
outline: Ask: whose voice has real authority in your life?
A synagogue in silence after the shout.
“O that today you would listen to his voice!”
live: Spend five minutes in silence with today's Gospel.
Bring one bondage or addiction to Jesus in confession.
Pray for priests, religious and consecrated people.
Do something kind for a young person in difficulty.
fathers: The demon confesses Christ but is rebuked: truth from a lying mouth is not welcome; let the Lord be confessed by those who love him.
The people were amazed at the new teaching; his authority was shown not only in words but in works.
magis: Christ is the fullness of revelation.
Jesus' signs and the defeat of Satan's reign.
Virginity for the Kingdom and marriage, both gifts of the Lord.
Celibacy as a gift and a sign.
saints: 1 Feb: weekday. 2 Feb: Presentation of the Lord (feast, World Day for Consecrated Life). 3 Feb: St Blaise (blessing of throats). 5 Feb: St Agatha. 6 Feb: St Paul Miki and companions.
2027-01-31.prayer: Grant us, Lord our God, that we may honour you with all our mind, and love everyone in truth of heart. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you teach with authority and free those who are bound. Speak to us today, let us not harden our hearts, and make us bearers of your freeing word to the young. Amen.

quick: God promised a prophet like Moses; Jesus is that prophet.
Jesus teaches with authority and commands unclean spirits.
Today, listen to his voice; do not harden your hearts.

catechism: The signs of the Kingdom; victory over Satan.

kidsaint: A priest in Italy who loved poor street boys. He taught them, played games with them and showed them Jesus. Lesson: we can help other children know Jesus through kindness and fun!

term: Greek for authority: the power that comes from who one is. Jesus teaches with exousia, not by quoting others.

family.explain: Jesus taught in the synagogue and everyone was amazed. A man with a bad spirit shouted, and Jesus said: be quiet, come out! And the man was free.
family.intention: We pray for all young people, through St John Bosco.

illus: A Salesian priest in Kochi runs a centre for boys who once lived at the railway station. One boy, addicted to glue, said after a year: on the street every voice told me what I was worth. At the centre I heard one voice that said I was God's son. That voice had authority. It set me free.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, speak to us with authority, and free us from all that binds us. Amen.
share: I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet (Deuteronomy 18:18). Do I hear Jesus as God's own voice?
He taught them as one having authority (Mark 1:22). Whose authority rules my choices?
O that today you would listen (Psalm 95:7). Where am I hardening my heart?
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim Christ's word with courage.
For those bound by addiction or evil.
For young people at risk, through St John Bosco.
For priests and consecrated men and women.
For our group, that we may not harden our hearts.
pm.close: God our Father, your Son speaks with authority and sets us free. Open our ears and soften our hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Moses promised Israel: the LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet (Deuteronomy 18:15). For centuries Israel waited.

In today's Gospel that prophet walks into the synagogue at Capernaum. The people were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes (Mark 1:22). The scribes quoted others; Jesus speaks as God's own Word.
Then a man with an unclean spirit cries out: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus says: be silent, and come out of him! And the spirit leaves (Mark 1:24–26). His word does what it says.
The people ask: what is this? A new teaching, with authority! (Mark 1:27). That same word is spoken to us at every Mass. It can free us from fear, from sin, from addiction, from all that binds.

The Psalm says: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts (Psalm 95:7–8). Paul speaks of unhindered devotion to the Lord. Married, single or consecrated, we are all called to give our hearts to him.
Today we would have honoured St John Bosco, who freed many young people by the word and love of Christ. Let us listen today, and let Jesus set us free. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus spoke and a bad spirit had to leave! Jesus' words are powerful.
Let us listen to Jesus today, and pray for all children, like St John Bosco did.

intro: Theme: “O that today you would listen to his voice!”
The prophet like Moses who teaches and frees with authority.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
points.apply: Read the Gospel as God's own voice.

q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
points.apply: Let Jesus' word, not opinion, guide one decision this week.

q: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!”
points.apply: Bring one bondage to Jesus in confession.

q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!
I say this for your own benefit, not to put any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence with the Gospel daily.

concl: Jesus is the prophet like Moses, the Word with authority.
His word frees; let us listen today.
